metric: Pairs proved equivalent by the algebraic prover over every database meeting the declared NOT NULL columns and keys; pairs a database shows different (label failures) leave the denominator.
correctness: 0 false proofs: every proof's two queries return the same rows on the generated TPC-H or TPC-DS data and on 150 small random databases plus the targeted suite
caveats: Logos 333d5275ac87; query text fetched at run time, never committed. By family: rbot-tpch 21/21 proved, 1 refuted; rbot-dsb 28/36 proved, 1 refuted; tpcds-variants 5/12 proved, 2 refuted. 14 TPC-DS variant pairs are adapted (TOP n read as LIMIT n, date + n days as an interval): 5 proved, 2 refuted among them. TPC-H data is scale 0.1 (tpchgen-cli); TPC-DS data is scale 1 from DSB's dsdgen, whose distributions differ from the official kit's. The TPC-H schema declares no keys, so proofs hold over every database with its NOT NULL columns. Prover routes time out after 120 s of wall-clock time, so a loaded machine can turn a few proofs into timeouts. Baseline before any harness fix: 23/69 proved, 4 refuted, 0 wrong (5/11 held out). The two harness fixes (moving Calcite's derived-table column lists into the derived table with KumoSQL's expand_alias_columns, and one renamed TPC-DS column on the generated data) were made on the dev split, but the baseline listing showed every pair's failure reason, held-out ones included (tuned on test, exposure only; the held-out score did not move). Measured on a3c22d2. 2026-11-13: the hardest-cases branch (Kumo_SQL_Prover PR 20) went from 43/69 on main (a23e844, same container, whole run; held out 7/11; 42/69 was recorded on 951be35) to 51/69 (held out 8/11) on a3c22d2, whose behaviour b389fe4 shares (it only replaces a per-rule closure with a module function). Nine pairs gained (rbot-tpch 13, 16; rbot-dsb 32, 54, 72 (held out), 81, 84, 92, 102) and one lost to the wall-clock limit (rbot-dsb 31, which proves alone on both trees at about two minutes with setup). Two pairs proved in an earlier run of the branch (rbot-dsb 1 and 30) are unknown now, as on main. The rules were written for Singh, LOGOS-shaped and conditional pairs; the rbot-dsb family is tuned on test because its queries are DSB templates, and no held-out case was read one by one. 2026-11-20 (the twelfth and thirteenth hardest-cases batches, Kumo_SQL_Prover PR 51): rerun on f9940a3 with nothing else running: the same 51 proofs, 0 wrong; one unknown pair (tpcds-variants query080) reaches the time limit now. 2026-11-23 (hardest-cases batches 19 to 24 and the fixes for issues 63 and 64, Kumo_SQL_Prover PR 62): the row is now the whole run on b923b93b, with nothing else running: 54/69, held out 8/11, 0 wrong. Main dd10806 run the same way in the same container proves 52: one tpcds-variants pair more than the 51 recorded on f9940a3 (which batch gained it was not traced). The two new proofs are rbot-dsb query001 and query030, which main declined as a regrouped FLOAT64 sum: they read a WITH query twice and add DECIMAL columns only, and the fix for issue 63 repairs the count. No proof is lost. One proof, tpcds-variants query018, takes 90 to 120 s against the 120 s limit on main and on this commit alike (the same 672 solver checks, timed in turn): it was cut off in two earlier whole runs of the branch and is proved in this one, so a run that cuts it off reads 53. The whole run on 8a0a7861 on 2026-11-24 (batches 25 and 26, PR 65, with development work beside it at the lowest priority) is such a run: 53 with every other proof in place, and query018 alone afterwards is proved in 97 s; tpcds-variants query080 and one held-out rbot-dsb pair, unknown before, reach the limit now. The row keeps the run of 2026-11-23.
